title: Teaching & Advising
text:
Advising & Mentoring
David chairs dissertation committees in the Education Policy program and serves on committees for students in Public Policy, Economics, and Measurement, Statistics, and Evaluation. He also mentors junior faculty and postdoctoral fellows in the department.
Prospective students interested in teacher labor markets, educator diversity, or causal inference in education are welcome to get in touch. Contact details are on the home page.

text: David also writes for policymakers, practitioners, and the public, including applied briefs for the Maryland Equity Project. That work is collected here. Peer-reviewed articles are on the Research page.

title: David Blazar
text:
Malen Professor for Urban Education PolicyCollege of Education, University of Maryland, College Park

Email  Download CV  Google Scholar
David Blazar is the Malen Professor for Urban Education Policy and an Associate Professor of Education Policy in the College of Education at the University of Maryland, College Park. He directs the Maryland Equity Project, leads the research branch of the Maryland Longitudinal Data System as principal investigator, and holds an affiliate appointment in the School of Public Policy.
His research asks how schools can use their resources, and especially their teachers, effectively and equitably. He studies what effective teachers do in the classroom, whether supports such as coaching, curricula, and evaluation actually improve teaching and student learning, and how labor market policies shape who enters teaching and who stays.
David began his career teaching high school English in New York City. He earned his doctorate in Quantitative Policy Analysis in Education and his master’s in Education Policy and Management at the Harvard Graduate School of Education.

title: Research
text: David’s research draws on education policy and economics. Using large administrative datasets and, where possible, experimental or quasi-experimental designs, he studies what makes teaching effective and how policy can help schools recruit, develop, and keep a strong and diverse teaching workforce. For a complete record, see his CV or Google Scholar profile.

title: Research
text:
Service and Affiliations
In addition to directing the Maryland Equity Project and leading the research branch of the Maryland Longitudinal Data System, David is a research affiliate of the CALDER Center. He serves on the editorial boards of Educational Researcher (since 2021) and the Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness (since 2025).
